cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the overseas job or opening this shop with me. You said we'd build something together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before I got the offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then decide what together means now. I'll run the counter if you'll still do the accounts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making a job abroad sound like leaving you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do the accounts from there, and we'll still build it together. Or take your money back and let me open it alone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 insists the job choice interpret a joint promise; A3 and A5 offer remote accounts to preserve the partnership while retaining a forced choice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 new offer causes A3 divided roles; B4 equating distance with goodbye causes A5 explicit overseas participation or money back.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 have coherent concerns about changed opportunity and emotional pressure.

heightening.evidence: A5 revises the choice so the old promise can mean building together from separate places or allowing A to open alone.

specificity.evidence: A1 shop not yet opened, A3 accounts and A5 money return establish concrete alternatives without metaphorical bookkeeping.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 pair of choices makes a practical demand rather than supplying a detached interpretation for the reader.
